Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$; $o$ is the manifold orientation, $N$ is a smooth future timelike field, and the metric volume form is chosen to agree with $o$. Let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected connection, let $\mathcal F$ be a smooth real two-form on $M$, and use the curvature convention
$R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z$.
Define
$$Q_{ab}(\mathcal F):=\mathcal F_{ac}\mathcal F_b{}^c-\frac14 g_{ab}\mathcal F_{cd}\mathcal F^{cd},$$
where both raised indices use $g^{-1}$. A **geometric electrovac datum with zero cosmological constant** is the tuple $(M,g,N,o,\mathcal F)$ satisfying
$$d\mathcal F=0,\qquad d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=2Q_{ab}(\mathcal F)$$
at every point of $M$. Here $\star_g$ is the Lorentzian Hodge map determined by $g$ and $o$; on two-forms $\star_g^2=-1$. No material current, matter tensor, global potential, asymptotic flatness, positive mass, horizon, or extension condition is part of this definition.

For an oriented embedded sphere $S$ on which the integrals converge, define its geometric electric and magnetic flux parameters by
$$q_e(S):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_S\star_g\mathcal F,\qquad q_m(S):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_S\mathcal F.$$
When $M$ and the coordinates have length units, these parameters have units of length. A magnetic flux need not have a global potential; no flux quantization is included. The background Lorentzian geometry and Hodge conventions carry the countable-choice assumption $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of their named suppliers; the algebraic identities in this definition require no additional choice principle.

Use the SI quantities, coordinate convention, and primitive/derived distinction of [[def-emg-geometry-units]], and the zero-cosmological-constant geometric electrovac flux normalization of [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]. This definition is the model-local parameter map for the RN and KN ansatz families; it is not a claim that nature contains an object with these parameters.

Take $G_N>0$, $c>0$, and $\mu_0>0$ as the gravitational and electromagnetic constants used by this coupled model, with $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. Let $m_*>0$ be a selected SI mass parameter in kg, $J\in\mathbb R$ a selected angular-momentum parameter in kg m$^2$ s$^{-1}$, $Q_e\in\mathbb R$ a selected electric charge parameter in C, and $\Phi_B\in\mathbb R$ a selected magnetic flux in Wb through an oriented sphere. These are the chosen SI inputs of this parametrization; this role is local to the solution families and is not a universal ontology for mass, angular momentum, or charge.

For the geometric flux integrals below, retain the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention explicitly stated by [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]] and defined by [[def-countable-choice]]. No arbitrary-index choice principle or magnetic-charge quantization is added.

Set

$$\alpha:=\sqrt{\frac{4\pi G_N}{\mu_0c^4}},\qquad \mathcal F:=\alpha F,$$

where $F$ is the SI electromagnetic two-form of [[def-emg-geometry-units]] and $\mathcal F$ is its geometric normalization. In length coordinates $F_{ab}$ has unit T, $\mathcal F_{ab}$ has unit m$^{-1}$, and $\alpha$ has unit T$^{-1}$m$^{-1}$. For an oriented sphere $S$, write the geometric flux parameters as

$$q_e:=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_S\star_g\mathcal F,\qquad q_m:=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_S\mathcal F.$$

The SI electric-flux convention is $Q_e=\varepsilon_0c\int_S\star_gF$, and the magnetic quantity used here is the flux $\Phi_B=\int_S F$. Thus

$$q_e=\frac{\alpha}{4\pi\varepsilon_0c}Q_e=\sqrt{\frac{G_N}{4\pi\varepsilon_0c^4}}\,Q_e,\qquad q_m=\frac{\alpha}{4\pi}\Phi_B.$$

The second equality in the electric formula uses the exact SI relation $\varepsilon_0\mu_0c^2=1$. Both $q_e$ and $q_m$ have units of length; $q_m$ is a flux parameter and is not assigned a universal SI magnetic-charge convention. If one separately chooses the convention $Q_m:=\Phi_B/\mu_0$ with unit A m, then the same definition reads $q_m=\sqrt{G_N\mu_0/(4\pi c^4)}\,Q_m$; this optional relabeling adds no new physical assumption or quantization rule.

For the metric parameters, set

$$M:=\frac{G_Nm_*}{c^2},\qquad a:=\frac{J}{m_*c},\qquad Q_{\mathrm{geom}}^2:=q_e^2+q_m^2.$$

Here $M$, $a$, $q_e$, and $q_m$ are derived length parameters, while $m_*$, $J$, $Q_e$, $\Phi_B$, $G_N$, $c$, and $\mu_0$ are the selected inputs of this map. The dimensionless metric coefficients use $M/r$, $a/r$, and $Q_{\mathrm{geom}}^2/r^2$. Horizon radii, areas, angular velocities, and surface gravities are further derived quantities of a specified solution, not additional primitive inputs.

These parameter identifications do not establish that $M$ equals an ADM or Komar mass, or that $J$ equals an ADM or Komar angular momentum; such identifications need their own global hypotheses and proofs. They supply no empirical values for $G_N$ or $\mu_0$, no measured black-hole parameters, no global potential in a nonzero magnetic-flux sector, and no claim of charge quantization. The source treatments use differing signatures, charge normalizations, and natural or Gaussian unit conventions; the SI formulas above are fixed by the stated local conventions and are not copied without conversion.

Adopt SI units and the following model-local quantity roles. Here the selected Einstein–Maxwell framework combines the stated Lorentzian geometry with a classical electromagnetic two-form and current; this definition itself supplies no gravitational equation, matter action, or empirical claim. A primitive is an input or independent field variable of this formulation; a derived quantity is fixed by a stated construction from its inputs. Neither label is universal across physical theories, and unit choice alone does not determine it.

The spacetime data are a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless four-manifold $M$, a smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, a smooth time-orientation field, and an independent orientation, exactly as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. The metric, its time orientation, and the manifold orientation are separate data. An observer at $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g(n,n)=-1$. A smooth observer congruence is a smooth field of such vectors. A local tetrad is a smooth basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with metric matrix $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$; an observer congruence, a coordinate chart, and a tetrad are different objects. Tetrads and observer fields need only exist locally; this definition assumes no global inertial chart, global tetrad, or hypersurface-orthogonal congruence.

The electromagnetic field-strength variable $F$ is a smooth real two-form, hence an alternating covariant tensor of type $(0,2)$, on an open subset of $M$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. It is primitive in this formulation. For an observer congruence $n$, its electric and magnetic observer covectors are derived by

$$E_a:=cF_{ab}n^b,\qquad B_a:=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b.$$

Here $\star_g$ is the unique Hodge map characterized pointwise by $\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$, using the metric and independent orientation, as in [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. Both covectors annihilate $n$ and lie in the rest covector space $\{\alpha\in T_p^*M:\alpha(n)=0\}$, whose induced metric is positive definite. In a positively oriented future orthonormal tetrad with $e_0=n$ and $\epsilon_{123}=+1$, their spatial components obey the fixed dictionary $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ from [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. Thus $E$ and $B$ are observer-dependent derived fields, not globally defined observer-independent three-vectors on a curved spacetime. Their tetrad components have units $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$ and tesla (T), respectively; the components of $F$ in a length-coordinate chart have unit T. No global potential is assumed; when a local potential $A_a$ is used, its components have unit $\mathrm{T\,m}$ and a scalar potential $\varphi$ has unit V.

For any chosen observer $n$, a smooth four-current is a vector field $j$ whose local decomposition is $j=c\rho\,n+J$, where $\rho:=-g(n,j)/c$ is the observer charge density and $J:=j-c\rho n$ is orthogonal to $n$. In the associated positively oriented orthonormal tetrad its components are $j^0=c\rho$ and $j^i=J^i$. The units are $[\rho]=\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, $[J^i]=[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, and $[q]=\mathrm C$ for a charge parameter supplied by a matter model. The current is a prescribed input or is supplied by an explicitly stated matter model; it is not inferred from the Maxwell equation alone.

The SI constants and coordinate units are fixed as follows. The speed of ideal vacuum light $c>0$ is the exact SI defining constant $299\,792\,458\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; identifying it with the shared ideal-light and clock conversion constant is the adopted Minkowski model of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]], not a consequence of its unit definition. The elementary charge $e$ is exactly $1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm C$. These unit definitions do not imply that charge is quantized. The magnetic constant $\mu_0>0$ has unit $\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$ and is experimentally determined in the revised SI, so no exact numerical value for $\mu_0$ is adopted. Define the electric constant (vacuum permittivity) $\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{F\,m^{-1}}$; hence $\varepsilon_0\mu_0c^2=1$, and $\varepsilon_0$ has the same relative standard uncertainty as $\mu_0$ because $c$ is exact. The exact component equation $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$ is dimensionally consistent: both sides have unit $\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$ in a length-coordinate frame.

In a length-coordinate chart all four coordinate values are assigned metres, with $x^0=ct$ when a time coordinate $t$ in seconds is selected. This is local coordinate bookkeeping, not a global inertial-coordinate claim. In such a chart $g_{ab}$ is dimensionless, the Levi-Civita coefficients $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ have unit $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, and curvature components have unit $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Components in other coordinate units transform by their Jacobians.

For the gravitational sector, take Newton's gravitational constant $G_N>0$ with unit $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$ and the cosmological constant parameter $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ with unit $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$ as primitive parameters of the selected model; no numerical value for either is used here. The coupling normalization $\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4$ is derived from these parameters and has unit $\mathrm{m\,J^{-1}}$. This definition records the convention for a later Einstein equation; it asserts no Einstein equation. A separate positive normalization $\kappa_0$ with unit weber (Wb) is a chosen flux conversion reserved for a later explicitly specified $U(1)$ formulation, where $U(1):=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ under multiplication. It is not $\kappa_E$, an electric charge, $\mu_0$, or Planck's constant, and it implies no charge quantization. Test-particle rest mass $m>0$ in kg and charge $q$ in C are externally supplied matter parameters, not quantities derived by classical electromagnetism.

These are SI and model-definition conventions only. They neither assert empirical measurements beyond the stated SI defining constants and measured status of $\mu_0$, nor identify similarly named quantities in another framework.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with signature
$(-,+,+,+)$, metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and oriented metric volume
form $\mathrm{vol}_g$. Let $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ be a smooth real two-form and
$j\in\Gamma(TM)$ a smooth vector field. Fix constants $\mu_0>0$ and $c>0$;
$\mu_0$ is a real coefficient here, and $c$ is the positive coordinate
conversion in $x^0=ct$ of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Assume the mathematical
field equations

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b.$$

The equations are conditional hypotheses, not physical postulates in this
mathematical item. Define $v\in\Gamma(TM)$ by $v^b:=\nabla_aF^{ab}$ and
define the current three-form by $\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$, the contraction
specified in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]. Then:

**(a) Sign identity.** On $M$,

$$d(\star_gF)=-\iota_v\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Consequently the sourced equation is equivalently

$$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

**(b) Current conservation.** Either equivalent sourced equation implies
$\nabla_aj^a=0$. This conclusion requires the sourced equation and $\mu_0>0$;
it does not require $dF=0$.

**(c) Local component check.** At any $p\in M$, choose a positively oriented
point-normal chart supplied by
[[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]. In that chart,
write $E_i(x):=-cF_{0i}(x)$ and
$B_i(x):=\frac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}(x)$, where $\epsilon_{123}=+1$ and
$\epsilon_{ijk}$ is alternating. These are local component abbreviations in
the chosen chart, not global observer fields. With
$\operatorname{div}E:=\partial_iE_i$,
$(\operatorname{curl}E)_k:=\epsilon_{kij}\partial_iE_j$, and similarly
for $B$, the pointwise component identities are

$$v^0=-\frac{1}{c}\operatorname{div}E,\qquad v^k=\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE_k-(\operatorname{curl}B)_k,$$

$$ (d\star_gF)_{123}=\frac{1}{c}\operatorname{div}E,\qquad (d\star_gF)_{0ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}\left(\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE_k-(\operatorname{curl}B)_k\right),$$

$$ (dF)_{123}=\operatorname{div}B,\qquad (dF)_{0ij}=\frac{\epsilon_{ijk}}{c}\left(\partial_tB_k+(\operatorname{curl}E)_k\right),$$

where $\partial_t:=c\,\partial_0$. The equations are pointwise identities
in normal coordinates; they do not assert that these component abbreviations
form global three-vector fields on curved spacetime.

On an open flat Minkowski domain with a fixed inertial Cartesian chart
$x^0=ct$, define $\rho:=j^0/c$, $J^i:=j^i$, and
$\epsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. The same component formulas at every point give

$$\operatorname{div}E=\frac{\rho}{\epsilon_0},\qquad \operatorname{curl}B-\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE=\mu_0J,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \partial_tB+\operatorname{curl}E=0.$$

These are a coordinate reduction of the stated tensor and form equations, not
claims that the smooth fields describe an experiment.

Let $M$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold of [[def-emg-geometry-units]], with metric $g$ of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ and the curvature convention of
[[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open. Take a smooth real
two-form $F$ and smooth current vector $j$ on $U$, with
$dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$ under the adopted convention of
[[post-emg-covariant-maxwell]]. A chosen smooth matter model supplies a smooth
symmetric covariant tensor $T^m_{ab}$ on $U$ and the current $j$; this postulate
does not assert that arbitrary independently prescribed $T^m$ and $j$ arise
from a matter model.

Define the Einstein tensor by $G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}
-\tfrac12 Rg_{ab}$, using the curvature contractions of
[[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], and define the smooth-field electromagnetic
stress tensor by

$$T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right).$$

For constant cosmological parameter $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and
$\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4$, adopt the additional equation-based gravitational
field law

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E\left(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab}\right).$$

Here $c>0$, $G_N>0$, and $\mu_0>0$ have the SI roles and units fixed in
[[def-emg-geometry-units]]; in length coordinates, $G_{ab}$ and
$\Lambda g_{ab}$ have units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, $T^{\mathrm{EM}}$ and $T^m$
have units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and $\kappa_E$ has units
$\mathrm{m\,J^{-1}}$. The source-free and sourced Maxwell equations remain
smooth-field postulates: point or sheet sources, distribution-valued products,
material excitation laws, and a global potential are outside this scope.

This is an equation-based adoption. It does not assume or imply the existence
of a matter action and is not derived from an action principle. The sources give
formulations in their own conventions; they motivate comparison but do not
establish a physical law or a solution-existence theorem.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Since $\alpha$ is constant, $dF=\alpha^{-1}d\mathcal F=0$ and $d(\star_gF)=\alpha^{-1}d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0$ by [F1]. Apply the sign identity [F4] to $F$: the vanishing of $d(\star_gF)$ gives $\iota_v\mathrm{vol}_g=0$, hence $v^b=\nabla_aF^{ab}=0$ at every point.

Contracting the definition of $Q$ in [F1] gives $g^{ab}Q_{ab}(X)=X_{ac}X^{ac}-(4/4)X_{cd}X^{cd}=0$. Therefore [F1] implies the scalar curvature is zero and $G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=2Q_{ab}(\mathcal F)$. Since $Q$ is quadratic and $\mathcal F=\alpha F$, this is $G_{ab}=2\alpha^2Q_{ab}(F)$.

Substituting $\alpha^2=4\pi G_N/(\mu_0c^4)$ from [F2] yields $G_{ab}=(8\pi G_N/c^4)Q_{ab}(F)/\mu_0=\kappa_ET^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}$. Together with step 1.1 and the specialization of [F5], these are exactly the adopted source-free equations. No equation is asserted at a removed point or outside the datum's domain, and the finite rescaling uses no choice beyond [A1].

The identity normalization alpha=1, when selected positive constants give that value in the chosen units, leaves F equal to the geometric form. Steps 1.1–2.1 still use 2alpha^2=kappa_E/mu_0; no exception at unit scale is introduced.
Statement: the metric is Lorentzian and nondegenerate under the exact geometric datum definition.
Statement: the claim is pointwise on the supplied open domain and makes no boundary extension.

Steps 1.1 and 1.2: A1 explicitly records AC_omega as inherited context. The proof multiplies the supplied two-form by the explicit positive alpha inverse and contracts four tensor indices; it chooses no family of fields.

Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and let $H\in C^\infty(D,(0,\infty))$ be independent of time. Write $x=(x^1,x^2,x^3)$ for length coordinates, set $x^0=ct$ when a time variable is used, and require $H$ to be dimensionless. The ordinary Euclidean Laplacian is $\Delta_\delta H:=\sum_{i=1}^3\partial_i^2H$; call $H$ harmonic when $\Delta_\delta H=0$. Take $\mathcal M=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times D$, with orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$ and future direction selected by $N_H=H\partial_{x^0}$.

For a sign $\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}$ define the metric and global potential one-form

$$g_H=-H^{-2}(dx^0)^2+H^2\sum_{i=1}^3(dx^i)^2,\qquad \mathcal A_\sigma=\sigma(H^{-1}-1)\,dx^0.$$

The associated two-form is

$$\mathcal F_\sigma:=d\mathcal A_\sigma=-\sigma\sum_{i=1}^3\frac{H_i}{H^2}\,dx^i\wedge dx^0,\qquad H_i:=\partial_iH.$$

The **positive harmonic conformastatic electrovac data** are the tuple $(\mathcal M,g_H,N_H,o,\mathcal F_\sigma)$ for these choices. The metric is the chart tensor of [[def-emg-conformastatic-chart-data]] and is Lorentzian with the stated future direction by [[lem-emg-conformastatic-chart-is-lorentzian]]. The term “electrovac data” names a candidate for the equations in [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]; this definition by itself does not assert that the equations hold. The field components have inverse-length units in length coordinates, so the Ricci and quadratic-field components both have inverse-length-squared units.

Let $N\ge1$ be an integer, let $a_1,\ldots,a_N\in\mathbb R^3$ be distinct, let $m_A>0$ have length units, and let $\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}$. On $D=\mathbb R^3\setminus\{a_1,\ldots,a_N\}$ define

$$H(x)=1+\sum_{A=1}^N\frac{m_A}{|x-a_A|}.$$

Then $H$ is smooth, positive and Euclidean harmonic on $D$, so [[def-emg-xs-harmonic-mp]] and [[thm-emg-xs-mp-verification]] give a smooth source-free geometric electrovac datum on $\mathbb R_{x^0}\times D$. For each $A$, every coordinate sphere $S_A(r)=\{x:|x-a_A|=r\}$ whose closed ball contains no other center has electric flux $q_e(S_A(r))=\sigma m_A$ and magnetic flux $q_m(S_A(r))=0$. If a coordinate sphere $S_R=\{x:|x|=R\}$ strictly encloses all centers, its fluxes are $q_e(S_R)=\sigma\sum_A m_A$ and $q_m(S_R)=0$. No center is included in the manifold; these are fluxes through regular spheres, not matter-source, horizon-extension, stability, or completeness claims.

Every datum of [[def-emg-xs-harmonic-mp]] satisfies the source-free geometric Einstein-Maxwell equations of [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]:

$$d\mathcal F_\sigma=0,\qquad d(\star_g\mathcal F_\sigma)=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=2Q_{ab}(\mathcal F_\sigma),\quad Q_{ab}(F):=F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\tfrac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}.$$

More explicitly, with $q_H:=\sum_iH_i^2$, the only nonzero independent raised field components are $\mathcal F^{i0}_\sigma=\sigma H_i/H^2$ and the quadratic-field components are

$$\mathcal F_{\sigma,ab}\mathcal F_\sigma^{ab}=-\frac{2q_H}{H^4},\qquad Q_{00}=\frac{q_H}{2H^6},\qquad Q_{0i}=0,\qquad Q_{ij}=\frac{\delta_{ij}q_H-2H_iH_j}{2H^2}.$$

of [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]] on a nonempty smooth four-manifold.
Thus $g$ has signature $(-,+,+,+)$, $\mathcal F$ is a smooth real two-form,
and
$$d\mathcal F=0,\qquad d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=2Q_{ab}(\mathcal F),\qquad Q_{ab}(X):=X_{ac}X_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}X_{cd}X^{cd}.$$

$x^0=ct$, $F_{ab}$ has units T, $\mathcal F_{ab}$ has units $\mathrm{m}^{-1}$,

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla^g_aF^{ab}=0,\qquad G_{ab}=\kappa_E T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}.$$

claims that the model describes nature.
